- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment pivot point, not trend continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates volatility in early days (e.g., days 1–5); reduce forecast by 1–2% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or bearish), model underperforms; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid underestimation.
